recuperate

rih-KOO-puh-rayt · verb

Hear It

What It Means

To recuperate is to recover strength or health after illness or exertion.

Grandpa spent the winter at the lake house, slowly recuperating from his long hospital stay.

Example

Following the concussion, the star player was ordered to recuperate at home for at least a month before any contact practice.

To recuperate is to regain your strength and health, usually gradually, after being sick, injured, or exhausted.

Your Turn

Compare the words

Synonyms · words with a similar meaning

recover: Recover is the broad, all-purpose word for getting something back -- you can recover your health, your balance, a lost wallet, or a lead in the polls, gradually or in an instant. To recuperate is narrower and slower: it means only the gradual rebuilding of strength and health.

heal: Heal centers on the body mending itself -- a cut heals, a broken bone heals, and we say time heals a grief. To recuperate is about the whole person: the weeks of resting and rebuilding strength that surround that mending after an illness or operation.

What it isn’t · antonyms and near-opposites

relapse: to fall back into a worse condition after improving

deteriorate: to become progressively worse

Where it sits · how structured the healing process is — rest → recuperate → rehabilitate

rest vs. recuperate: Rest is any everyday break, tied to nothing in particular, while to recuperate is to rest with a job to do: rebuilding strength after illness, injury, or exhaustion.

rehabilitate vs. recuperate: To rehabilitate is a longer, more structured process of restoring full function, often after serious injury -- a bigger undertaking than simply recuperating.

Build the Word

The pieces

prefix — re-

prefix — re-: back (Latin)

root — cuper-

root — cuper-: to take, to get (from Latin recuperare, 'to get back,' related to capere, 'to take, to seize')

suffix — -ate

suffix — -ate: forms a verb (Latin)

Put it together

Put it together: Recuperate is built from re- ('back') + cuper- ('to take, to get,' from Latin recuperare, related to capere, 'to take, to seize') + -ate (a verb ending) -- literally 'to take back,' which fits perfectly: to recuperate is to take back the strength or health you had lost.
